source_text: In which OSI layer does a network switch generally operate? The Data Link layer

source_text: Which network topology has a higher security risk: bus, ring, star, or wireless? Wireless

source_text: In which OSI layer does language translation for applications occur? The Presentation layer

source_text: The session layer is NOT responsible for which: modulation, relating two end users, identifying users? Modulation/demodulation

source_text: Breaking a single connection can disrupt the whole network in which topology? Ring

source_text: Ethernet is an example of which topology? Bus topology

source_text: Which serves the largest geographical region: LAN, WAN, MAN, or PAN? WAN

front: Find \(a\) so that \(B = 3a x i + 2y j - 2z k\) is a valid magnetic field.
source_text: Find \(a\) so that \(B = 3a x i + 2y j - 2z k\) is a valid magnetic field. \(a = 0\)   (\(\nabla \cdot B\) must be \(0\))

front: Which can be a magnetic field: \(A = 2x^{2} i + y j + 3z^{2} k\) or \(B = 2y^{2} i + 3x j - 2xy k\)?
source_text: Which can be a magnetic field: \(A = 2x^{2} i + y j + 3z^{2} k\) or \(B = 2y^{2} i + 3x j - 2xy k\)? \(B\)   (its divergence is \(0\))

front: Given induced \(E = 2yz i + 3x^{2}y j + x^{2}y^{2} k\), find \(\dfrac{\partial B}{\partial t}\) (\(= -\nabla \times E\)).
source_text: Given induced \(E = 2yz i + 3x^{2}y j + x^{2}y^{2} k\), find \(\dfrac{\partial B}{\partial t}\) (\(= -\nabla \times E\)). \(-2x^{2}y i - (2y - 2xy^{2}) j - (6xy - 2z) k\)

front: Curl of the E field induced by \(B = -\cos^{2}(3t) k\).
source_text: Curl of the E field induced by \(B = -\cos^{2}(3t) k\). \(-6 \cos(3t) \sin(3t) k\)

source_text: Magnetic flux density inside a torus, radius \(2\ \text{cm}\), \(50\) turns, \(1\ \text{A}\). \(\approx 500\ \mu\text{T}\)   (\(B = \dfrac{\mu N I}{2\pi r}\))

source_text: Total current in a wire producing \(0.1\ \text{T}\) at a radial distance of \(20\ \text{cm}\) (in air). \(\approx 100\ \text{kA}\)   (\(I = \dfrac{B \cdot 2\pi r}{\mu}\))

source_text: E field at the origin from \(Q_1 = 50\ \text{nC}\) at \((0,1,0)\) and \(Q_2 = -50\ \text{nC}\) at \((0,-1,0)\). \(\approx 900\ \text{V/m}\) (directed along \(-y\))

source_text: E field between two infinite parallel plates with charge densities \(+\rho_s\) and \(-\rho_s\). \(\dfrac{\rho_s}{\varepsilon}\)

source_text: E field midway between two infinite parallel wires (\(+2\ \text{C/m}\) and \(-1\ \text{C/m}\), \(1\ \text{m}\) apart). \(\approx 1\times10^{11}\ \text{V/m}\)

source_text: Reflection coefficient at a \(300 + 50j\ \Omega\) load on a \(100\ \Omega\) line. \(\approx 0.51\angle{6.9^{\circ}}\)   (\(\Gamma = \dfrac{Z_L - Z_0}{Z_L + Z_0}\))

source_text: Standing wave ratio for a \(50\ \Omega\) line with a \(500 + 25j\ \Omega\) load. \(\approx 10\)

source_text: Load on a \(250\ \Omega\) line if the standing wave ratio is \(2\). \(500\ \Omega\)   (\(Z_L = Z_0 \times \text{SWR}\))

source_text: Contact potential of a p-n junction: \(N_a = N_d = 2\times10^{15}\ \text{/m}^{3}\), \(n_i = 1\times10^{10}\ \text{/m}^{3}\), \(T = 300\ \text{K}\). \(\approx 0.634\ \text{V}\)   (\(V_0 = \dfrac{kT}{q} \ln\left(\dfrac{N_a N_d}{n_i^{2}}\right)\))

source_text: Balanced Wheatstone bridge with \(R_1 = 100\ \Omega\), \(R_2 = 1000\ \Omega\), \(R_3 = 500\ \Omega\). Find \(R_x\). \(5000\ \Omega\)   (\(R_x = \dfrac{R_2 R_3}{R_1}\))

source_text: Real power in a \(2\ \Omega\) resistor if \(2\ \text{C}\) of charge passes through it in \(1\ \text{s}\). \(8\ \text{W}\)   \((I = 2\ \text{A},\ P = I^2R)\)

source_text: Force between \(Q_1 = 10\times10^{-6}\ \text{C}\) and \(Q_2 = 100\times10^{-6}\ \text{C}\) separated by \(1\ \text{cm}\). \(\approx 90\ \text{kN}\)   \((F = kQ_1Q_2/r^2)\)

source_text: Potential difference between plates \(1\ \text{m}\) apart with field strength \(2000\ \text{V/m}\). \(2000\ \text{V}\)   \(V = Ed\)

source_text: Potential difference for a charge accelerated \(200\ \text{m}\) in a \(1\ \text{kV/m}\) field. \(200\ \text{kV}\)   \(V = Ed\)

front: Charge on a \(0.01\ \text{kg}\) particle suspended between plates \(0.1\ \text{m}\) apart at \(100\ \text{V}\).
source_text: Charge on a \(0.01\ \text{kg}\) particle suspended between plates \(0.1\ \text{m}\) apart at \(100\ \text{V}\). \(\approx 9.81\times10^{-5}\ \text{C}\)   \((Q = mgd/V)\)

front: Angle between a \(0.1\ \text{m}\), \(5\ \text{A}\) conductor and a \(10\ \mu\text{T}\) field if the force is \(1\ \mu\text{N}\).
source_text: Angle between a \(0.1\ \text{m}\), \(5\ \text{A}\) conductor and a \(10\ \mu\text{T}\) field if the force is \(1\ \mu\text{N}\). \(\approx 11.5^{\circ}\)   \((F = BIL\sin\theta)\)

front: Voltage across a parallel-plate capacitor: \(400\ \mu\text{C}\), \(A = 0.02\ \text{m}^2\), \(d = 0.01\ \text{m}\).
source_text: Voltage across a parallel-plate capacitor: \(400\ \mu\text{C}\), \(A = 0.02\ \text{m}^2\), \(d = 0.01\ \text{m}\). \(\approx 22.6\times10^{6}\ \text{V}\)   \((C = \varepsilon A/d,\ V = Q/C)\)

front: Constant charging current: a \(100\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor rises from \(5\ \text{V}\) to \(10\ \text{V}\) over 3 minutes.
source_text: Constant charging current: a \(100\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor rises from \(5\ \text{V}\) to \(10\ \text{V}\) over 3 minutes. \(\approx 2.7\ \mu\text{A}\)   \((I = C\Delta V/\Delta t)\)

front: Energy stored in a \(200\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor with \(v(t) = 240\sin(377t)\ \text{V}\).
source_text: Energy stored in a \(200\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor with \(v(t) = 240\sin(377t)\ \text{V}\). \(5.76\sin^2(377t)\ \text{J}\)   \((E = \tfrac{1}{2}Cv^2)\)

source_text: Voltage induced in a \(5\ \text{mH}\) inductor as current rises 0 to \(100\ \text{mA}\) in \(2\ \text{ms}\). \(0.25\ \text{V}\)   \((V = L\,di/dt)\)

source_text: Energy stored in a \(100\ \text{mH}\) inductor carrying \(i(t) = t^2\) at \(t = 10\ \text{s}\). \(500\ \text{J}\)   \((i = 100\ \text{A},\ E = \tfrac{1}{2}Li^2)\)

front: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\sin^{2}(x)\cdot(\cot^{2}(x)+1)\).
source_text: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\sin^{2}(x)\cdot(\cot^{2}(x)+1)\). \(1\)  (since \(\cot^{2}x+1=\csc^{2}x=\dfrac{1}{\sin^{2}x}\))

front: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\dfrac{\cot^{2}(x)}{\cot^{2}(x)+1}\).
source_text: Simplify the trigonometric expression: \(\dfrac{\cot^{2}(x)}{\cot^{2}(x)+1}\). \(\cos^{2}(x)\)

source_text: Simplify: \((\sin x+\cos x)^{2}-1\). \(\sin(2x)\)

front: Express \((8+4j)-(5+0j)\) in polar form.
source_text: Express \((8+4j)-(5+0j)\) in polar form. \(5\angle{53^{\circ}}\)   (\(=3+4j\))

front: Express \(\dfrac{4+4j}{2+3j}\) in polar form.
source_text: Express \(\dfrac{4+4j}{2+3j}\) in polar form. \(\approx 1.57\angle{-11^{\circ}}\)

front: Express \(2\angle{30^{\circ}}\times 4\angle{15^{\circ}}\) in rectangular form.
source_text: Express \(2\angle{30^{\circ}}\times 4\angle{15^{\circ}}\) in rectangular form. \(8\angle{45^{\circ}}=5.7+5.7j\)

front: Express \(4\angle{30^{\circ}}+6\angle{30^{\circ}}\) in rectangular form.
source_text: Express \(4\angle{30^{\circ}}+6\angle{30^{\circ}}\) in rectangular form. \(\approx 8.66+5j\)

front: In what three forms can \(3+4j\) be written?
source_text: In what three forms can \(3+4j\) be written? Rectangular \(5(\cos 53^{\circ}+j\sin 53^{\circ})\), Euler \(5e^{j53^{\circ}}\), and polar \(5\angle{53^{\circ}}\)

front: Find the complex conjugate of \(Z=(2+6j)(3+3j)\).
source_text: Find the complex conjugate of \(Z=(2+6j)(3+3j)\). \(-12-24j\)   (since \(Z=-12+24j\))

front: Find the 35th term of the arithmetic progression \(2, 4, 6, 8, \dots\)
source_text: Find the 35th term of the arithmetic progression \(2, 4, 6, 8, \dots\) \(70\)   (\(a_n=a+(n-1)d=2+34\cdot 2\))

front: Sum of a 120-term arithmetic progression with first term 1 and last term 259.
source_text: Sum of a 120-term arithmetic progression with first term 1 and last term 259. \(15{,}600\)   (\(S=\dfrac{n(a+l)}{2}\))

front: Find the 12th term of the geometric progression \(3, 9, 27, 81, \dots\)
source_text: Find the 12th term of the geometric progression \(3, 9, 27, 81, \dots\) \(531{,}441\)   (\(a_n=a\cdot r^{n-1}=3\cdot 3^{11}\))

front: Sum of a geometric progression with first term 1, last term 19683, ratio 3.
source_text: Sum of a geometric progression with first term 1, last term 19683, ratio 3. \(29{,}524\)   (\(S=\dfrac{a-r\cdot l}{1-r}\))

front: Find the angle between the lines \(y=x+4\) and \(y=5x+6\).
source_text: Find the angle between the lines \(y=x+4\) and \(y=5x+6\). \(\approx 33.7^{\circ}\)   (\(\tan^{-1}\left|\dfrac{m_2-m_1}{1+m_1\cdot m_2}\right|=\tan^{-1}(4/6)\))

front: Find the equation of the line through \((2,10)\) and \((3,12)\).
source_text: Find the equation of the line through \((2,10)\) and \((3,12)\). \(y=2x+6\)

front: Write the equation of a line with slope 2 and y-intercept -5.
source_text: Write the equation of a line with slope 2 and y-intercept -5. \(y=2x-5\)

back: Any line of slope \(-1/4\), e.g. \(y=-x/4\) or \(y=-x/4+4\)
front: Give a line perpendicular to \(y=4x+4\).
source_text: Give a line perpendicular to \(y=4x+4\). Any line of slope \(-1/4\), e.g. \(y=-x/4\) or \(y=-x/4+4\)

front: A conic-section equation with only an \(x^{2}\) term (or only a \(y^{2}\) term) is what conic?
source_text: A conic-section equation with only an \(x^{2}\) term (or only a \(y^{2}\) term) is what conic? A parabola
What conic is \(2(x-10)^{2}+8(y-6)^{2}=200\)? An ellipse

front: Find the eccentricity of the ellipse \(2(x-10)^{2}+8(y-6)^{2}=200\).

source_text: What conic is \(2(x-10)^{2}-8(y-6)^{2}=200\)? A hyperbola

front: Find the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(2(x-10)^{2}-8(y-6)^{2}=200\).
source_text: Find the eccentricity of the hyperbola \(2(x-10)^{2}-8(y-6)^{2}=200\). \(\approx 1.1\)   (\(e=\sqrt{1+b^{2}/a^{2}}\), \(a=10\), \(b=5\))

front: What conic is \((y-8)^{2}=4(x-2)\)?
source_text: What conic is \((y-8)^{2}=4(x-2)\)? A parabola

front: Volume of a right circular cylinder with radius 1 m and height 2 m.
source_text: Volume of a right circular cylinder with radius 1 m and height 2 m. \(\approx 6.28\ \text{m}^{3}\)   (\(V=\pi r^{2}h\))

front: Surface area of a right circular cone with radius 2 m and height 4 m.
source_text: Surface area of a right circular cone with radius 2 m and height 4 m. \(\approx 40.6\ \text{m}^{2}\)   (\(A=\pi r(r+\sqrt{r^{2}+h^{2}})\))

front: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\tan^{2}(x)+\sin^{2}(x)\).
source_text: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\tan^{2}(x)+\sin^{2}(x)\). \(4\tan(x)\sec^{2}(x)+2\sin(x)\cos(x)\)

front: Differentiate \(f(x)=4x^{2}+6x+2y^{2}\) with respect to \(x\).
source_text: Differentiate \(f(x)=4x^{2}+6x+2y^{2}\) with respect to \(x\). \(8x+6\)

front: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\tan(x)\sec(x)\).
source_text: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\tan(x)\sec(x)\). \(2(\tan^{2}(x)\sec(x)+\sec^{3}(x))\)

front: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\sin^{-1}(x)+2\cos^{-1}(x)\).
source_text: Differentiate \(f(x)=2\sin^{-1}(x)+2\cos^{-1}(x)\). \(0\)   (the derivatives cancel)

back: Local min at \(x=1/3\); local max at \(x=-1/2\)
front: Find local min/max of \(f(x)=4x^{3}+x^{2}-2x+8\) on \(-1\lt x\lt 1\).
source_text: Find local min/max of \(f(x)=4x^{3}+x^{2}-2x+8\) on \(-1\lt x\lt 1\). Local min at \(x=1/3\); local max at \(x=-1/2\)

back: Local min at \(x=1/3\); local max at \(x=-1\)
front: Find local min/max of \(f(x)=3x^{3}+3x^{2}-3x+3\) on \(-2\lt x\lt 1\).
source_text: Find local min/max of \(f(x)=3x^{3}+3x^{2}-3x+3\) on \(-2\lt x\lt 1\). Local min at \(x=1/3\); local max at \(x=-1\)

front: Find the point of inflection of \(f(x)=3x^{3}+3x^{2}-3x+3\).
source_text: Find the point of inflection of \(f(x)=3x^{3}+3x^{2}-3x+3\). \(x=-1/3\)   (where \(f''=18x+6=0\))

front: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to \pi/2}\dfrac{4\cos x}{2-2\sin x}\).
source_text: Evaluate \(\lim_{x\to \pi/2}\dfrac{4\cos x}{2-2\sin x}\). \(\infty\)   (L'Hopital \(\to 2\tan x\))

front: Evaluate the integral \(\int \dfrac{4}{x+3}\,dx\).
source_text: Evaluate the integral \(\int \dfrac{4}{x+3}\,dx\). \(4\ln|x+3|+C\)

front: Evaluate the integral \(\int (\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x)\,dx\).
source_text: Evaluate the integral \(\int (\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x)\,dx\). \(x+C\)

front: Solve the first-order ODE \(y'+2x^{2}y=x^{2}\).
source_text: Solve the first-order ODE \(y'+2x^{2}y=x^{2}\). \(y=1/2+Ce^{-2x^{3}/3}\)
Solve \(y''+6y'+9y=0\). \(y=(C_1+C_2 x)e^{-3x}\)   (repeated root \(r=-3\))

front: Is \(2y''+4y'+8y=0\) over-, under-, or critically damped?
source_text: Is \(2y''+4y'+8y=0\) over-, under-, or critically damped? Underdamped   (\(a^{2}=4\lt 4b=16\))

front: Classify the equation \(y''+8y'+12y=0\).
source_text: Classify the equation \(y''+8y'+12y=0\). 2nd-order linear homogeneous differential equation

back: No - matrix addition requires identical dimensions
front: Can a \(3\times 3\) matrix be added to a \(2\times 2\) matrix?
source_text: Can a \(3\times 3\) matrix be added to a \(2\times 2\) matrix? No - matrix addition requires identical dimensions

front: Find the determinant of \([[4,5],[2,6]]\).
source_text: Find the determinant of \([[4,5],[2,6]]\). \(14\)

back: No - columns of A (2) must equal rows of B (3)
front: Can \(A\ (3\times 2)\) be multiplied by \(B\ (3\times 2)\)?
source_text: Can \(A\ (3\times 2)\) be multiplied by \(B\ (3\times 2)\)? No - columns of A (2) must equal rows of B (3)

back: No - matrix multiplication is not commutative
front: Is \(A\times B=B\times A\) true for all matrices?
source_text: Is \(A\times B=B\times A\) true for all matrices? No - matrix multiplication is not commutative

front: Find the dot product of \(A=2i+j+3k\) and \(B=i+2j+4k\).
source_text: Find the dot product of \(A=2i+j+3k\) and \(B=i+2j+4k\). \(16\)

front: Find the cross product \(A\times B\) for \(A=3i+2j+k\) and \(B=i+4j+0k\).
source_text: Find the cross product \(A\times B\) for \(A=3i+2j+k\) and \(B=i+4j+0k\). \(-4i+j+10k\)

front: Sample standard deviation of \(2, 4, 6, 8\).
source_text: Sample standard deviation of \(2, 4, 6, 8\). \(\sqrt{20/3}\approx 2.58\)

front: Sample geometric mean of \(1, 2, 3, 4\).
source_text: Sample geometric mean of \(1, 2, 3, 4\). \((24)^{1/4}\approx 2.21\)

source_text: Root mean square (RMS) of \(3, 5, 6, 11\). \(\approx 6.9\)   (\(\sqrt{191/4}\))
Median of \(90, 60, 70, 110, 50, 40, 200, 210\). \(80\)   (mean of the two middle values)

Given a customer is under 30, find \(P(\text{prefers online})\).
source_text: 20% shop online (50% under 30); 80% in-store (40% under 30). Given a customer is under 30, find \(P(\text{prefers online})\). \(\approx 0.24\)   (Bayes: \(0.10/0.42\))

front: \(P(\text{hire})=0.10\) per interview. Find \(P(\text{exactly 2 hires in 30 interviews})\).
source_text: \(P(\text{hire})=0.10\) per interview. Find \(P(\text{exactly 2 hires in 30 interviews})\). \(\approx 0.228\)   (binomial)

front: \(P(\text{win each slam})=0.40\) for 4 slams. Find \(P(\text{winning 2 to 4})\).
source_text: \(P(\text{win each slam})=0.40\) for 4 slams. Find \(P(\text{winning 2 to 4})\). \(\approx 0.51\)   (binomial, \(k=2,3,4\))

front: GMAT scores are normal with mean 740, sd 20. Find \(P(\text{score}\lt 700)\).
source_text: GMAT scores are normal with mean 740, sd 20. Find \(P(\text{score}\lt 700)\). \(\approx 0.0228\)   (\(z=-2\))

front: Dishwasher life is normal with mean 10 yr, sd 2 yr. Find \(P(\text{lasts 12 to 14 yr})\).
source_text: Dishwasher life is normal with mean 10 yr, sd 2 yr. Find \(P(\text{lasts 12 to 14 yr})\). \(\approx 0.1359\)   (\(z\) from 1 to 2)

source_text: Fund gains -5%, 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% with \(p=0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.30, 0.10\). Find the expected performance. \(\approx 5.5\%\)

front: A study-time pdf is \(f(x)=4x-1\) for \(0\lt x\lt 1\) (else 0). Find \(E[X]\).
source_text: A study-time pdf is \(f(x)=4x-1\) for \(0\lt x\lt 1\) (else 0). Find \(E[X]\). \(5/6\)   (\(\int_{0}^{1} x(4x-1)\,dx\))

front: A pdf is \(f(x)=2x^{-3}\) for \(x\gt 1\) (else 0). Find \(E[X]\).
source_text: A pdf is \(f(x)=2x^{-3}\) for \(x\gt 1\) (else 0). Find \(E[X]\). \(2\)   (\(\int_{1}^{\infty} x\cdot 2x^{-3}\,dx\))

front: What is the total area under any pdf (or total sum under a pmf)?
source_text: What is the total area under any pdf (or total sum under a pmf)? 1

front: Income mean $55,000, \(\sigma\) = $5,000, \(n = 60\), normal. Find the 99% confidence interval for the mean.
source_text: Income mean $55,000, \(\sigma\) = $5,000, \(n = 60\), normal. Find the 99% confidence interval for the mean. $55,000 \(\pm\) $1,662

front: With \(\sigma\) = $5,000 and \(n = 60\), find the standard error of the mean (SEM).
source_text: With \(\sigma\) = $5,000 and \(n = 60\), find the standard error of the mean (SEM). \(\approx\) $645   \((\sigma/\sqrt{n})\)

front: \(n = 10\), mean \(100\ \text{min}\), \(s = 20\ \text{min}\), t-distribution. Find the 90% confidence interval for the mean.
source_text: \(n = 10\), mean \(100\ \text{min}\), \(s = 20\ \text{min}\), t-distribution. Find the 90% confidence interval for the mean. \(100 \pm 11.5\)

front: For \(n = 10\), mean 100, \(s = 20\) at 90% (t), what is the margin of error?
source_text: For \(n = 10\), mean 100, \(s = 20\) at 90% (t), what is the margin of error? ≈ 11.5

back: An anode, a cathode, and an electrolyte
front: What three things must be present for corrosion to occur?
source_text: What three things must be present for corrosion to occur? An anode, a cathode, and an electrolyte

front: Diffusion coefficient with \(D_0 = 7.8\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\), \(Q_d = 250\ \text{J/mol}\), \(T = 973\ \text{K}\).
source_text: Diffusion coefficient with \(D_0 = 7.8\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\), \(Q_d = 250\ \text{J/mol}\), \(T = 973\ \text{K}\). \(\approx 7.6\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\)   \((D = D_0\exp(-Q_d/RT))\)

front: Activation energy for \(D = 1.3\times10^{-22}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\) given \(D_0 = 2.7\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\) at \(T = 773\ \text{K}\).
source_text: Activation energy for \(D = 1.3\times10^{-22}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\) given \(D_0 = 2.7\times10^{-5}\ \text{m}^2/\text{s}\) at \(T = 773\ \text{K}\). \(\approx 256\ \text{kJ/mol}\)   \((Q_d = -RT\ln(D/D_0))\)

front: Resistivity of a \(100\ \text{m}\) wire, \(2\ \text{mm}\) diameter, with \(5\ \Omega\) resistance.
source_text: Resistivity of a \(100\ \text{m}\) wire, \(2\ \text{mm}\) diameter, with \(5\ \Omega\) resistance. \(\approx 1.57\times10^{-7}\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}\)   \((\rho = RA/L)\)

back: Area of A must be \(4\times\) the area of B
front: Cable A's resistivity is \(4\times\) cable B's. For equal resistance and length, how must their areas compare?
source_text: Cable A's resistivity is \(4\times\) cable B's. For equal resistance and length, how must their areas compare? Area of A must be \(4\times\) the area of B

front: Magnetic permeability of a medium where a \(100\ \text{A}\) infinite wire gives \(0.5\ \text{T}\) at \(0.5\ \text{m}\).
source_text: Magnetic permeability of a medium where a \(100\ \text{A}\) infinite wire gives \(0.5\ \text{T}\) at \(0.5\ \text{m}\). \(\approx 0.015\ \text{H/m}\)   \((\mu = B\cdot 2\pi r/I)\)

front: Maximum weight a \(2\ \text{mm}\)-diameter rod supports if ultimate tensile strength is \(2000\times10^{8}\ \text{Pa}\).
source_text: Maximum weight a \(2\ \text{mm}\)-diameter rod supports if ultimate tensile strength is \(2000\times10^{8}\ \text{Pa}\). \(\approx 628\ \text{kN}\)   \((F = \text{UTS}\times\text{area})\)

front: Young's modulus: a \(100\ \text{N}\) load stretches a \(10\ \text{m}\), \(1\ \text{mm}\)-diameter wire by \(2\ \text{mm}\).
source_text: Young's modulus: a \(100\ \text{N}\) load stretches a \(10\ \text{m}\), \(1\ \text{mm}\)-diameter wire by \(2\ \text{mm}\). \(\approx 6.36\times10^{11}\ \text{N/m}^2\)   \((E = (F/A)/(\Delta L/L))\)

front: True strain of a material that stretches \(20\ \text{mm}\) from an original length of \(200\ \text{mm}\).
source_text: True strain of a material that stretches \(20\ \text{mm}\) from an original length of \(200\ \text{mm}\). \(\approx 0.095\)   \((\ln(220/200))\)

front: Thermal strain of steel (\(\alpha = 1.2\times10^{-5}\ /^{\circ}\text{C}\)) heated from \(20\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\) to \(45\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\).
source_text: Thermal strain of steel (\(\alpha = 1.2\times10^{-5}\ /^{\circ}\text{C}\)) heated from \(20\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\) to \(45\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\). \(3\times10^{-4}\) (\(30\times10^{-5}\))   \((\varepsilon = \alpha\Delta T)\)

front: Temperature coefficient if a specimen's resistance doubles over a \(25\ \text{K}\) rise.
source_text: Temperature coefficient if a specimen's resistance doubles over a \(25\ \text{K}\) rise. \(0.04\ /\text{K}\)   \(((R_2/R_1 - 1)/\Delta T)\)

front: Z-transform of \(x[n] = 0.2^{n} u[n]\).
Z-transform of the sequence \(x[n] = [2, 3, 1, 0, 5]\).
Z-transform of \(x[n] = 5 (0.75^{n}) u[n]\).
Inverse Z-transform of \(X(z) = \dfrac{z}{z - 0.5}\).
source_text: Inverse Z-transform of \(X(z) = \dfrac{z}{z - 0.5}\). \(0.5^{n} u[n]\)

front: Minimum sampling frequency for \(\text{sinc}(1000\pi t) + \text{sinc}(2000\pi t)\).
source_text: Minimum sampling frequency for \(\text{sinc}(1000\pi t) + \text{sinc}(2000\pi t)\). \(2000\ \text{Hz}\)   (highest component \(1000\ \text{Hz}\); Nyquist \(= 2\times\))

front: Sampling \(\cos(3000\pi t + \theta)\) at \(2000\ \text{Hz}\) produces what?
source_text: Sampling \(\cos(3000\pi t + \theta)\) at \(2000\ \text{Hz}\) produces what? Aliasing (\(f_s = 2000 \lt 2 \times 1500\ \text{Hz}\))

front: Aliased frequency of \(\cos(400\pi t + \theta)\) sampled at \(300\ \text{Hz}\).
source_text: Aliased frequency of \(\cos(400\pi t + \theta)\) sampled at \(300\ \text{Hz}\). \(100\ \text{Hz}\)   (\(|200 - 300|\))

back: Sampling at or above the Nyquist rate AND an ideal low-pass filter

source_text: What is required for complete reconstruction of a band-limited signal? Sampling at or above the Nyquist rate AND an ideal low-pass filter

front: Which type of digital filter is non-recursive?
source_text: Which type of digital filter is non-recursive? Finite Impulse Response (FIR)

front: Which type of digital filter is recursive?
source_text: Which type of digital filter is recursive? Infinite Impulse Response (IIR)

front: Digital filtering does NOT involve which: sampling, A/D, D/A, or phase modulation?
source_text: Digital filtering does NOT involve which: sampling, A/D, D/A, or phase modulation? Phase modulation

front: Trace \(x=0,\ y=0,\ z=10\); do-while\((z \gt 0)\){ \(y=y+1;\ x=2y-1;\ z=z-3\) }. Final value of \(x\)?
source_text: Trace \(x=0,\ y=0,\ z=10\); do-while\((z \gt 0)\){ \(y=y+1;\ x=2y-1;\ z=z-3\) }. Final value of \(x\)? 7

front: Spreadsheet: \(B4 = A4 + C4\), with \(A4 = 25\) and \(C4 = A4 \times 4 = 100\). Value of \(B4\)?
source_text: Spreadsheet: \(B4 = A4 + C4\), with \(A4 = 25\) and \(C4 = A4 \times 4 = 100\). Value of \(B4\)? 125

front: Efficiency of binary search as a function of \(n\) comparisons?
source_text: Efficiency of binary search as a function of \(n\) comparisons? \(\log_2(n)\)

source_text: Which sorting algorithm has the best worst-case time: bubble, insertion, or heap? Heap sort \((n \cdot \log_2 n)\)

front: Which is NOT a phase of the Software Development Lifecycle: testing, implementation, deployment, or marketing?
source_text: Which is NOT a phase of the Software Development Lifecycle: testing, implementation, deployment, or marketing? Marketing

source_text: A design that tends to break in unrelated places when changed is called? Fragile

source_text: A good software design displays what quality? It can be extended without modifying the original design

source_text: Static software testing verifies through what? Program code review

front: Dynamic software testing verifies through what?
source_text: Dynamic software testing verifies through what? Program code execution

front: The "top-down" approach is most applicable to which programming style?
source_text: The "top-down" approach is most applicable to which programming style? Structured programming

front: The concept of a "class" is most applicable to which programming style?
source_text: The concept of a "class" is most applicable to which programming style? Object-oriented programming

front: Which is NOT a structured-programming language: FORTRAN, BASIC, COBOL, or C#?
source_text: Which is NOT a structured-programming language: FORTRAN, BASIC, COBOL, or C#? C# (it is object-oriented)
